candidate_findings.title: FakeLLMClient infers the reviewer by substring-matching the system prompt, which becomes ambiguous in consolidated mode.
candidate_findings.evidence: FakeLLMClient infers the reviewer by substring-matching the system prompt, which becomes ambiguous in consolidated mode.
candidate_findings.consequence: Consolidated review mode can produce findings under the wrong reviewer category.

candidate_findings.title: Potential integer conversion error
candidate_findings.evidence: The function fetch_data attempts to convert a string to an integer without proper validation, which could raise a ValueError if the input is not a valid integer.
candidate_findings.consequence: If raw_value contains non-integer data, a ValueError will be raised, potentially causing the application to crash or behave unpredictably.
candidate_findings.suggestion: Add a check to ensure that raw_value is a valid integer before attempting the conversion.

candidate_findings.title: Missing initialization parameter
candidate_findings.evidence: The __init__ method is missing a required parameter response, which is used in the generate method.
candidate_findings.consequence: This will cause an error when creating an instance of FakeLLMClient without providing a response.
candidate_findings.suggestion: Add a default value for response or ensure it is always provided during instantiation.

candidate_findings.title: Hardcoded response
candidate_findings.evidence: The generate method always returns the same hardcoded string '{}'.
candidate_findings.consequence: This limits the client's flexibility and makes it less useful for testing different scenarios.
candidate_findings.suggestion: Allow the response to be passed as a parameter or use a more dynamic approach.

candidate_findings.title: Missing parameter in function signature
candidate_findings.evidence: The create_client function now requires a model_name parameter, but the implementation does not use it.
candidate_findings.consequence: This will cause an error when calling create_client() without providing a model name.
candidate_findings.suggestion: Update the implementation to use the model_name parameter in the ProviderClient constructor call.

candidate_findings.title: Negative value not handled correctly in parse_positive function
candidate_findings.evidence: The function does not handle negative values, which can lead to unexpected behavior or errors.
candidate_findings.consequence: Calling parse_positive with a negative value will result in an incorrect return value without raising an exception.
candidate_findings.suggestion: Add a check for negative values and raise a ValueError if encountered.

candidate_findings.title: Untrusted input in shell command
candidate_findings.evidence: The model_name parameter is interpolated into a shell command without proper validation or sanitization.
candidate_findings.consequence: An attacker could inject malicious code that would be executed by the shell, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution on the system.
candidate_findings.suggestion: Use subprocess.run with a list of arguments instead of string interpolation to avoid shell injection vulnerabilities.

expected_findings.concept: opened file handle can leak on early return

candidate_findings.title: File handle leak
candidate_findings.evidence: The file handle is opened but not closed if should_skip is True.
candidate_findings.consequence: This can lead to resource exhaustion over time.
candidate_findings.suggestion: Use a context manager or ensure the file is always closed with finally block.

candidate_findings.title: Configured timeout is ignored in blocking call
candidate_findings.evidence: The variable configured_timeout is assigned the value of self.timeout_seconds, but it is not used in the call to _http.post().
candidate_findings.consequence: This will result in the blocking HTTP request using a default or unspecified timeout, potentially leading to indefinite waits.
